question: According to current official Bun documentation, how can Bun.WebView connect to an already-running browser over a browser-level CDP WebSocket URL, and which lifecycle operations are documented?

claims.text: Bun's WebView docs show connecting to an already-running Chrome-family browser by passing a `backend` object with `type: "chrome"` and a Chrome DevTools WebSocket `url` such as `ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/...` to `new Bun.WebView(...)`.

evidence_passages.text:
new Bun.WebView(options?) #

Option Type Default Description

width number 800 Viewport width in CSS pixels. Range 1-16384.

height number 600 Viewport height in CSS pixels. Range 1-16384.

url string — Begin navigating to this URL immediately.

headless boolean true Only true is implemented; false throws.

backend "webkit" | "chrome" | object "webkit" on macOS, "chrome" elsewhere Rendering engine.

console typeof console | (type, ...args) => void — Capture page-side console.* calls. See Console capture .

dataStore "ephemeral" | { directory: string } "ephemeral" Storage for cookies / localStorage / IndexedDB. See Persistent storage .

backend object form #

Option Type Description

type "chrome" | "webkit" Required. Which engine to use.

path string ( chrome only) Path to the Chrome/Chromium executable. Forces spawn mode.

argv string[] ( chrome only) Extra launch flags, appended after the defaults. Forces spawn mode.

url string | false ( chrome only) ws:// URL of an existing Chrome's DevTools endpoint, or false to skip auto-detect and always spawn. See above .

claims.text: The docs say the Chrome `backend.url` option is a Chrome-only `ws://` URL for an existing Chrome DevTools endpoint, and `url: false` disables auto-detect and forces Bun to spawn its own browser instead.
acceptable_patterns: Chrome `backend\.url` option is a Chrome-only `ws://` URL

claims.text: The docs say Bun may auto-detect an already-running Chrome-family browser by reading `DevToolsActivePort` from standard profile directories; if found, Bun connects over WebSocket instead of spawning a new browser.
acceptable_patterns: connects over WebSocket instead of spawning

evidence_passages.text: If auto-detect finds a stale DevToolsActivePort file (Chrome crashed or restarted), the WebSocket connect fails and Bun transparently falls back to spawning its own Chrome. An explicit url: "ws://..." does not fall back — a failed connection throws.

claims.text: The docs say `url: "ws://..."` cannot be combined with `path` or `argv`, and passing `path` or `argv` implies spawn mode and skips auto-detect.
acceptable_patterns: passing `path` or `argv` implies spawn mode and skips auto-detect

rejected_claims.text: The explicit lifecycle operations are only `close()` and `Bun.WebView.closeAll()` because other lifecycle sections are behaviors rather than operations.
rejected_claims.reason: The supplied evidence labels this as the author's interpretation rather than a verbatim Bun statement.

rejected_claims.text: The example `ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/...` is specifically a browser-level CDP WebSocket URL.
rejected_claims.reason: The supplied evidence says this wording is a synthesis, not Bun's exact phrasing.

rejected_claims.text: No conflicting statement was found in the official Bun WebView docs reviewed.
rejected_claims.reason: This is a search/review outcome, not a stable product-doc claim about Bun.WebView itself.

rejected_claims.text: No separate official Bun page adds more lifecycle operations beyond `close()` and `Bun.WebView.closeAll()`.
rejected_claims.reason: This is framed as reviewer uncertainty and absence-of-evidence, not a documented Bun claim.

rejected_claims.text: The docs say that if an explicit `url: "ws://..."` connection fails, Bun does not fall back to spawning a browser and instead throws the connection failure.
rejected_claims.reason: required concept is absent from teacher-run evidence: no_fallback

rejected_claims.text: The documented lifecycle operations are instance `close()` and class `Bun.WebView.closeAll()`. The docs also say `view[Symbol.dispose]` and `view[Symbol.asyncDispose]` both point to `close()` for automatic cleanup.
rejected_claims.reason: claim text is not lexically grounded in teacher-run evidence
